title: Divisorial fine saturated log regular pairs
statement: Let $V$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $Z\subseteq V$ a closed subset [def-pc-scheme] with dense open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow V$. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $M=\mathcal O_V\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$: on an etale $W\to V$, this consists of regular functions on $W$ whose restriction to $W\times_V U$ is invertible, with multiplication and its inclusion into $\mathcal O_V$. This is the divisorial log structure of $(V,Z)$. A chart is an etale-local homomorphism $P\to M$ from a commutative monoid for which, at each geometric point $\bar v$ [def-weil-geometric-point] with strict local ring $A$, writing $\alpha:P\to A$ for the composite of the chart with $M_{\bar v}\to A$, the induced map $P\oplus_{\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\to M_{\bar v}$ is an isomorphism; the displayed pushout identifies the elements of $P$ mapping to units with those units. Here the strict local ring is the stalk $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}$, the colimit of rings of sections on pointed etale neighbourhoods, and $M_{\bar v}$ is the stalk of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. A commutative monoid $P$ is fine saturated if it is finitely generated, embeds in its group completion $P^{\rm gp}$, and $g\in P^{\rm gp}$ and $ng\in P$ for some integer $n>0$ imply $g\in P$. The log structure is fine saturated if it has such charts. The pair $(V,Z)$ is log regular if this log structure is fine saturated, its triviality locus (where $M_{\bar v}=A^\times$) is exactly $U$, and at every geometric point $\bar v$ the following holds. Put $\overline M_{\bar v}=M_{\bar v}/A^\times$ and let $I\subseteq A$ be generated by the images of the nonunits of $M_{\bar v}$. Then $A/I$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}(\overline M_{\bar v}^{\rm gp})$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and rank means dimension after tensoring the abelian group with $\mathbf Q$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q121-7aeb047bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item against ILO Exposé VI 1.1–1.4 (pp. 69–70). The definition is correct. Its regularity condition, dim A = dim A/I + rank of the characteristic monoid's group, is Kato's form (Kato 1994, Def. 2.1), which ILO 1.3 says is equivalent to the étale definition. The extra 'dense complement' hypothesis is harmless: by ILO 1.4 a log regular pair already has a dense open complement, and every citer satisfies it. Small cases test as expected: Z empty (log regular iff V regular), the crossing xy=0 in A^2 (log regular), the origin in A^2 (fails because the trivial locus is too large), and the cusp (fails because A/I is not regular). There are no new nodes. There is no duplicate in the DAG and no blueprint node for it (rg over all three blueprint snapshots), and the Mathlib searches are recorded. As a definition it has no route or tool_uses. The fix covers three missing citations (point B3): geometric point -> def-weil-geometric-point, étale stalks (the colimit over pointed étale neighbourhoods) -> def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, and Krull dimension -> def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, all added to stmt_deps and checked for cycles. It also defines the symbol α, which the statement used without introducing. The meaning of the definition is unchanged.
